notes: §1985:IX.1.3.4 lists the logic error statuses of an indexed file: 41 ("An OPEN statement is attempted for a file in the open mode"), 42 ("A CLOSE statement is attempted for a file not in the open mode"), 43 (in the sequential access mode the last input-output statement before a DELETE or REWRITE "was not a successfully executed READ statement"), 44 (a write or rewrite of a record "larger than the largest or smaller than the smallest record allowed for the RECORD IS VARYING clause"; in level 1 a rewrite of a record "not the same size as the record being replaced"), 46 (a sequential READ when "no valid next record has been established" after an unsuccessful START, an unsuccessful READ or an at end), 47 (READ or START "on a file not open in the input or I-O mode"), 48 (WRITE "on a file not open in the I-O, output, or extend mode") and 49 (DELETE or REWRITE "on a file not open in the I-O mode"). The runtime is one path for every edition (a program compiled at --std 85 calls the same connector entries, and none of these members reads the edition): FileConnector.OpenOnce answers 41 for an open connector and Close 42 for a closed one; the Status setter drops the successful-READ gate at every operation's outcome and ReadSucceeded alone re-arms it, so IndexedConnector.Rewrite and Delete answer 43 under sequential access only, after MutationOpenModeGuard's 49; KeyedConnector.RecordRulesFailure with FileConnector.Stored answers 44 for a WRITE or REWRITE outside the VARYING bounds; Unsuccessful and InvalidateFilePosition invalidate the position at every failed READ and START, and SequentialReadGuard and ReadSequential answer 46 until a successful START or READ (ReadRandom included) re-establishes it; ReadOpenModeGuard and StartOpenModeGuard answer 47 and Write 48. The level-1 arm of 44 does not apply: the compiler implements level 2, where §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR3 lets the sizes differ (a REWRITE of 14 characters over 10 is 00). One answer lies outside the rule: a sequential-access WRITE on a file open I-O is 48, the later editions' §2023:9.1.13.7 GR8 a); 1985 does not permit that statement (§1985:IX.4.4.4 GR4, Table 2: sequential WRITE under output and extend only) and names no status for it, so no arm of the rule is contradicted. Probed at --std 85 on indexed files: 41 on OPEN OUTPUT and OPEN INPUT of an open file; 42 on a second CLOSE; 43 on REWRITE and DELETE with no READ, after a REWRITE, a DELETE, a START, a failed READ and a refused (44) REWRITE, and 00 after a READ; no 43 under dynamic access; 44 at 7 and 15 characters of a VARYING 8 TO 14 file on WRITE and REWRITE (20 and 3 under sequential access), and 00 at 8 and 14; 46 after a failed START, after at end and after a failed random READ, and 00 again after a successful START or random READ; 47 on READ and START of a closed, an output and an extend file; 48 on WRITE of a closed and an input file and 00 on a dynamic-access WRITE under I-O; 49 on REWRITE and DELETE of a closed, an output and an input file and on REWRITE of an extend file. The witness shows 42 for a CLOSE of a file never opened and 41 for a second OPEN OUTPUT, each through its USE procedure.

next.reason: 41, 42, 43, 46, 47, 49 keep their 1985 cases (46: an at-end READ is an unsuccessful READ, §2023:9.1.13.7 GR6 b) 'The preceding READ statement referencing that file connector was unsuccessful'; 41/42 add only DELETE FILE/UNLOCK). Two results differ. 1985 g. 'WRITE ... on a file not open in the I-O, output, or extend mode' gives no 48 for a sequential-access WRITE in I-O mode; §2023:9.1.13.7 GR8 a) 'If the access mode is sequential, the file connector is not open in the extend or output mode' gives 48. And 1985 d.2) 'rewrite a record to an indexed file and the record is not the same size' (44) is gone: 44 b) now covers only 'a sequential file' (§2023:9.1.13.7 GR4) and §2023:14.9.35.4 GR18 says for relative and indexed files the size 'may differ from the number of bytes in the record being replaced'.
